_comment: Config-forced ENUM probe. Both `attrTypes` enum override forms are exercised, because
for a long time NEITHER reached the phantom emitters and there was no test to say so.
`Attr.fromOverride` classified every enum override to `Attr.AEnumMap`, and `AEnumMap`
was matched at ZERO sites in Generate/Phantom/{Emit,Model}.elm — only `AEnum` was. So
an override fell through every `case` to the `_ ->` default and emitted a plain
`String -> Attr` setter: no union row, no `<Lib>.Values` tokens, no constraint at all.
An author who deliberately narrowed an attribute to three values got exactly the
surface they would have got by not writing the override.
The fix has two halves and this fixture pins both:
- LIST form (`Bar.disable-pagination`) — all pairs are identity, so `fromOverride`
normalizes it to `AEnum`, the variant the pipeline already understood.
- MAP form (`Gate.strict`) — at least one pair differs, so it stays `AEnumMap` and
the pipeline has to carry the token/value split all the way to `Ir.token`.
`Bar.mode` is not incidental either: its CEM enum mints `auto` into the brand-wide
token pool, and BOTH overrides then ask for an `auto` token. They must REUSE it. A
duplicate identifier in `<Lib>.Values` is a hard COLLISION error the generator raises
on purpose (there is an `error-case` suite that depends on that), so if pooling broke,
this fixture would fail the run rather than emit something subtly wrong.

Bar._comment_attrTypes: LIST form: token == value for every entry. `auto` is already in the pool from the `mode` enum and must be reused.

Gate._comment_attrTypes: MAP form: the KEY is the Elm token name, the VALUE is the string written to the DOM. `always` writes "true" and `never` writes "false" — the whole reason this form exists — while `auto` is an identity pair sharing the pooled token.
